title: 🧹 [code health improvement] Use `unknown` instead of `any` in catch blocks
description:
🎯 **What:** The type of the caught error in `try...catch` blocks within `app/kontrol/page.tsx` was changed from `any` to `unknown`.

💡 **Why:** Using `any` bypasses TypeScript's type checking, making it unsafe to access properties like `.message` on the error object without validation. Changing it to `unknown` and applying an `instanceof Error` check (`err instanceof Error`) forces the code to explicitly assert the shape of the error object before using it, increasing type safety and maintainability.

✅ **Verification:** 
- Verified the application passes TypeScript compilation checks successfully without any typing errors.
- Verified that the full test suite passes with all 115 unit and integration tests passing.
- Requested a code review which confirmed the modifications to `app/kontrol/page.tsx` correctly applied type checks and successfully substituted string outputs for instances of error printing.

✨ **Result:** Improved the strictness of error checking inside `app/kontrol/page.tsx`, bringing it in line with `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` rules and improving overall type safety.
